title: At the Gym
goal: Ask about membership and classes, decide whether to join, and request help during a first visit.

rows.text: Someone who guides a person's exercise training.
A group exercise session / the person leading it.
A class using stationary exercise bikes.
A practice involving postures, movement and breathing.
A method using controlled movements, on a mat or with special equipment.
High-intensity interval training: periods of hard exercise alternating with recovery periods.
A class learning or practicing dance movements.

runs.text: Class names help you ask about the activity.
What does this class involve?
and
Is there a class for beginners?
let the instructor explain the particular session rather than leaving you to guess from its name.
This fictional gym supplies the facts for the chapter:

rows.text: $10; gym access for that day; classes cost extra.
$40 each month; no joining fee; gym access and cycling classes included; renews automatically.
$6 per class, including for monthly members.
Available by separate appointment; ask staff for the price.

runs.text: For this monthly plan, staff require a cancellation request at least seven days before the next renewal. This is a scene condition, not a rule for all gyms.
Renewal
continues a membership;
automatic
renewal happens under the arrangement without a new purchase request each month.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Hi. I'm interested in joining. Could you explain the membership options?

turns.en: Hi. I'm interested in joining. Could you explain the membership options?

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: A day pass is ten dollars. Monthly membership is forty, with no joining fee.

turns.en: A day pass is ten dollars. Monthly membership is forty, with no joining fee.

runs.text: Are classes included?

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Cycling is included in the monthly plan. Yoga is six dollars per class.

turns.en: Cycling is included in the monthly plan. Yoga is six dollars per class.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Does the monthly plan renew automatically?

turns.en: Does the monthly plan renew automatically?

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Yes. To cancel before a renewal, we need your request at least seven days beforehand.

turns.en: Yes. To cancel before a renewal, we need your request at least seven days beforehand.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Could I have those terms in writing before I decide?

turns.en: Could I have those terms in writing before I decide?

runs.text: Of course.

blocks.caption: Ask about the membership · Visitor & Staff

runs.text: Included
means part of the stated price.
Extra
means additional.
Is there a joining fee?
How do I cancel?
, and
Can I pause the membership?
ask different questions; one answer does not settle all three.
Other useful inquiries are
Could I have a tour?
Where are the locker rooms?
Can I book a personal trainer?
, and
Do you offer women-only sessions?
The staff can explain availability and conditions. The fictional card does not answer the last question, so leave its answer open.

study.title: Decide without being pushed into agreement

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Would you like to sign up today?

turns.en: Would you like to sign up today?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: I'd like to try a day pass first.

turns.en: I'd like to try a day pass first.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Sure. Would you like a class as well?

turns.en: Sure. Would you like a class as well?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Not today. Just the day pass, please.

turns.en: Not today. Just the day pass, please.

blocks.caption: Decide without being pushed into agreement · Staff & Visitor

runs.text: Sign up
means register or join.
I'd like to join
makes a positive decision.
I'm just looking today
or
I don't want to sign up today
states a different intention. You can ask for time to compare options:
I'll think about it and get back to you.
That does not confirm a membership.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Hi. I'm here for the cycling class. It's my first time.

turns.en: Hi. I'm here for the cycling class. It's my first time.

turns.speaker: Instructor

runs.text: Welcome. We'll use bike five for you today.

turns.en: Welcome. We'll use bike five for you today.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Could you show me how to adjust it?

turns.en: Could you show me how to adjust it?

turns.speaker: Instructor

runs.text: Yes, I'll show you before we start.

turns.en: Yes, I'll show you before we start.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: And how should I let you know if I need a break?

turns.en: And how should I let you know if I need a break?

runs.text: Just tell me.

blocks.caption: Attend a first class · Participant & Instructor

runs.text: It's my first time
identifies the help you may need.
Could you repeat that more slowly?
repairs an instruction.
I need a break
states a need;
I'd like to watch first
requests a different way to begin. These are communication choices, not exercise instructions.
With another participant:
Have you taken this class before? — A few times.
Their experience can start a conversation without proving that the class is suitable for you.
Use the gym card. Alone, say the staff or instructor lines and then your own replies; with a partner, exchange roles.
Ask about the monthly price, a joining fee, cycling and yoga. As staff, answer only from the card. Confirm which class costs extra.
Ask how to cancel before a renewal. Staff give the seven-day condition. Repeat the condition and request it in writing.
Staff ask whether you want to join. Choose a monthly membership, a day pass, or no purchase. Say your choice clearly.
Arrive for your first cycling class and ask about adjusting the bike. Then change the cue: you did not understand an instruction. Ask for repetition.
You want a personal-training appointment, but the price is unknown. Ask about cost and availability without inventing an answer.
Possible responses:

“So cycling is included, but yoga is six dollars extra?” / “You need the cancellation request at least seven days before renewal. Could I have that in writing?” / “Just a day pass today, please.” / “Could you repeat the instruction more slowly?” / “What does a personal-training session cost, and when could I book one?”
Cover the models later and change the class or decision.
Check:
Did you distinguish the membership, an extra charge, an unconfirmed inquiry and your actual choice? Could you ask for help instead of pretending to understand?
